title: Transferring a design with carbon paper
subtitle: The dressmaker's carbon paper method for transferring a design onto any fabric.
excerpt: Dressmaker's carbon paper transfers a design to fabric by pressing through it with a stylus or empty ballpoint pen. The coloured carbon lifts onto the fabric surface and stays through most of the stitching, then washes out.
sourceNotes: Carbon paper transfer for embroidery was documented in needlework periodicals from the 1880s onward. Principles consistent with Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776.

glossaryTerms.definition: The method of placing dressmaker's carbon paper between a design and the fabric, then tracing the design lines with a stylus to transfer the coloured marks onto the cloth below.

content.text: works by placing carbon paper, coloured side down, between the design and the fabric. Tracing the design lines presses the carbon dye from the paper onto the cloth. The transferred marks stay through stitching and wash out with the finished piece.

items.name: Blunt stylus or empty ballpoint pen

content.text: Choose a carbon colour that contrasts with the fabric: white or yellow on dark fabric, blue or red on light fabric.
Place the fabric on a firm surface. Lay the carbon paper on top, coloured side down.
Lay the design on top of the carbon paper, right side up.
Secure all three layers with tape or pins at the corners. Do not allow them to shift during tracing.
Trace all the design lines firmly with a blunt stylus. Apply steady pressure but don't tear through the paper.
Lift a corner to check the transfer before removing everything.

items.cause: Not enough pressure was applied, or the carbon paper is old.
items.fix: Press more firmly. Test on a scrap first to check the carbon is still active.

items.symptom: The layers shifted and the design is smeared
items.cause: The layers were not secured before tracing began.
items.fix: Always tape or pin all three layers before starting. Remove tape only after tracing is complete.

content.text: Carbon paper transfer works on any fabric, including those too thick for light-box tracing. It suits velvet and pile fabrics where a water-soluble pen will not mark the pile.
